title: Anthropic's CCA Exam as a Field-Guide for Agentic Engineering — Frank Coyle, UC Berkeley
talk_summary: Frank Coyle uses Anthropic's CCA exam scenarios to catalog agentic engineering anti-patterns: unchecked loops, overloaded agents, context spill, interactive CI, and unbounded context. He recommends stop-reason loops, specialized subagents, context isolation/compaction, critic slices, batch mode, and non-interactive pipelines.

takeaways.what_they_do: Loop on model responses and branch on stop_reason: execute tool when tool_use, stop on end_turn, and handle max_tokens instead of accepting partial output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to loop with something called the stop reason

takeaways.what_they_do: Give each subagent one job and only the one or two tools it needs, rather than loading one agent with every tool.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you can get your agents to do one thing, you with maybe one or two tools available to it

takeaways.technique: Critic gets claim and evidence only
takeaways.what_they_do: For review/critic subagents, pass only the claim and evidence, not the producing agent's full thought process, to avoid groupthink and context pollution.
Submit prompts as a batch for 50% fewer token cost with results promised in at least 24 hours.
takeaways.numbers: 50% fewer token cost; at least 24 hours

takeaways.what_they_do: Configure CI agent runs to proceed without interactive permission prompts; interactive mode in a pipeline stalls.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Always have interactive modes in a pipeline. Well, no no no
